causes.claim: The v2.31.0 release likely caused the 502s by setting the application keepalive timeout to 60 seconds while nginx kept upstream connections open for 75 seconds. Requests sent on connections nginx still considered open could fail after the application had closed them.

citations.title: Postmortem: checkout-api 502 errors after release v2.31.0
citations.section: Postmortem: checkout-api 502 errors after release v2.31.0
citations.quote:
The release replaced the application server's default keepalive timeout of 120 seconds with an
explicit value of 60 seconds. The nginx sidecar keeps upstream connections for 75 seconds.

citations.title: Postmortem: checkout-api 502 errors after release v2.31.0
citations.section: Postmortem: checkout-api 502 errors after release v2.31.0
citations.quote:
For 15
seconds out of every 75 the application had already closed a connection that nginx still considered
open, and a request sent on it failed with a 502.

causes.claim: The orders-api write connection pool is likely exhausted. A likely mechanism is transactions being left open, leaving connections idle in transaction until the pool runs out; the evidence does not establish whether that is happening in this incident.

citations.title: orders-api database connection pool exhausted
citations.section: orders-api database connection pool exhausted
citations.quote:
A large number of `idle in transaction` sessions means the application opened a transaction and
   did not finish it. This is the most common cause.

citations.title: orders-api database connection pool exhausted
citations.section: orders-api database connection pool exhausted
citations.quote: A request waits up to 30 seconds for a free connection (`pool_timeout=30`)

causes.claim: The indexer may be exceeding its memory limit because its batch size is too large; the runbook says batches of 5000 need far more than the pod’s 2Gi limit.

citations.title: search-indexer pods OOMKilled

citations.quote: a batch of 5000 documents needs far more than the limit.

causes.claim: A recent indexing-library change could have increased per-document memory use enough to trigger OOM kills, even with a batch size of 1000. The evidence does not establish whether that change occurred in this incident.

causes.claim: The billing release introduced a retry helper that generated a fresh idempotency key for each attempt. When an initial charge succeeded but timed out, a retry with a different key created a second charge.

citations.section: Postmortem: annual subscribers charged twice
citations.quote:

timestamp.

citations.title: Postmortem: annual subscribers charged twice
citations.section: Postmortem: annual subscribers charged twice
citations.quote:

second charge

causes.claim: The v2.31.0 rollout shortened checkout-api’s keepalive timeout below nginx’s, so nginx reused connections the app had already closed and returned 502s.

causes.claim: The immediate cause is likely an exhausted orders-api database connection pool: write requests are waiting for a connection and timing out. Idle-in-transaction sessions are a common underlying cause, though the incident evidence does not confirm that they are present here.

causes.claim: The likely issue is in regional session validation for users in Germany, such as a problem with the regional Redis cluster or its network path. The notification worker is less likely to be the cause because notifications are still arriving.
